11b_1_work_of_the_sums.png: The number of terms of the Lovelock sums for the 64 components of $P_{(k)}$ of the corrected metric, order $k = 1$ to $4$, on a logarithmic vertical axis: all index lists of the literal formula (grey), the ordered products of $k$ of the 112 nonzero curvature entries (purple), the combinations left after skipping those with a repeated label (blue), and the ones for which GKD is called (orange). For $k = 3$ the literal sum has about $4.4 \times 10^{12}$ terms, of which only 322,560 are evaluated; for $k = 4$ nothing is left, because nine labels out of eight must repeat.
11b_2_curvature_of_planes.png: The curvature $K(a, b) = R^{ab}_{\ ab}$ of the plane of the coordinate directions $x_a$ and $x_b$ of the corrected metric, in units of $H^2$, as exact fractions: left at the moment $x_4 = 0$ of the history of the record, where $a_4^{\prime} = H$, $u = 4H/3$, $k = 1$ and $a_4^{\prime\prime} = v = 0$; right at the same moment with $a_4^{\prime\prime} = v = H^2$; red positive, blue negative, the diagonal empty. Planes in 3-space have 1, planes of 3-space with $x_0$ or an extra time $-1/3$, planes inside the block of $x_0, x_5, x_6, x_7$ have $(a_4^{\prime} - u/2)^2 - H^2 k = -8/9$; only the planes with the time $x_4$ change on the right, where $a_4^{\prime\prime}$ and $v$ enter.
11b_3_riemann_matrix.png: All 4096 components of the Riemann tensor $R^{ab}_{\ \ cd}$ of the corrected metric at the moment $a_4^{\prime} = H$, $u = 4H/3$, $k = 1$, $a_4^{\prime\prime} = v = H^2$, arranged as a 64 by 64 table: row $8a + b$ is the upper pair of labels, column $8c + d$ the lower pair, counted from 0; red positive, blue negative, white zero. Only 112 components are not zero, and each lies on the main diagonal, the curvature $R^{ab}_{\ \ ab}$ of a coordinate plane, or at its mirrored place $R^{ab}_{\ \ ba} = -R^{ab}_{\ \ ab}$: no component mixes two different planes.
11b_4_mixing_terms_vanish.png: Why the corrected metric has no curvature component that mixes the time $x_4$ with the hidden direction $x_0$: for each direction $c$ of 3-space and of the extra times the component $R^{x_4 c}_{\ \ x_0 c}$ is the product of the rate $\partial_0 \ln f_c$ of its scale factor along $x_0$ (blue, in units of $H \cot z$) and the difference $\partial_4 \ln f_c - \partial_4 \ln f_0$ of its rate in time and that of the hidden direction (orange, in units of $H$, at the moment $x_4 = 0$ of the history of the record). For 3-space the first factor is 0, for the extra times the second, because they share the scale factor $e^{-a_4} b_4^{1/2}$ of the hidden direction: every product is 0, for every history and every real $z$.
11b_5_lovelock_component_tables.png: All 64 components $E_{(k)}{}^h{}_j$ of the normalised Lovelock tensors $E_{(1)} = G$ (left), $E_{(2)}$ (middle) and $E_{(3)}$ (right) of the corrected metric at the moment $x_4 = 0$ of the history of the record, where $a_4^{\prime} = H$, $u = 4H/3$, $k = 1$ and $a_4^{\prime\prime} = v = 0$, in units of $H^2$, $H^4$ and $H^6$, as exact fractions; row $h$, column $j$; red positive, blue negative, white zero, each table on its own colour scale. Only the diagonal is filled, so the $x_4$-$x_0$ components vanish; the three space entries are equal, and the hidden entry $x_0$ equals the three extra-time entries, for example $-2/3$ for Einstein's tensor.
